negative: Place malformed command delimiters or unsupported value-change tokens in the file.
positive: Parse a VCD containing every declaration and simulation command, scalar/vector/real changes, all time units, and representative variable types.

edge: Exercise endpoint characters ! and ~.
negative: Use whitespace or a character outside ASCII 33-126 in a code.
positive: Validate generated one- and multi-character identifier codes against the allowed range.

edge: Dump signed negative values of each type.
negative: Use host-native C widths instead of fixed SystemVerilog widths.
positive: Dump one variable of each type and verify exact legacy type and size.

edge: Use $comment in each context permitted by the full grammar.
negative: Use a simulation-only dump keyword as a declaration command.
positive: Place every declaration keyword in the declaration region and every simulation keyword in simulation data.

edge: Include optional whitespace and comment sections between required sections.
negative: Treat manually inserted conforming keyword commands as invalid solely due to origin.
positive: Parse equivalent keyword sections produced automatically and manually.

edge: Extend a one-character value to a wide vector.
negative: Sign-extend a leading 1 with ones.
positive: Parse shortened values beginning in each of 0, 1, X, and Z and verify restored prefixes.

edge: Select a scope containing both individual variables and a memory.
negative: Include strength or memory value records in a 4-state VCD.
positive: Dump a strength-bearing net and verify only its logic state; verify memory contents are absent.

edge: Use nested packed aggregates with opposing index directions.
negative: Emit separate VCD dimensions or fields.
positive: Dump multidimensional packed arrays and packed structs and verify one flat vector of total width.

edge: Use zero, subnormal, very large, and sign-varying values.
positive: Dump real values requiring near-full binary64 precision and round-trip them through %g parsing.

edge: Dump a one-bit vector and a scalar.
negative: Encode a non-real variable using real-number syntax.
positive: Dump real, scalar, and vector values containing every four-state symbol.

edge: Use multi-character identifier codes.
negative: Insert whitespace between scalar value and identifier.
positive: Validate records such as 1! or xA with immediately adjacent identifier codes.

edge: Nest several differing scope types.
negative: Use an unsupported scope type.
positive: Generate declarations for each supported scope type and verify its keyword.

edge: Generate an increment in which no selected variable changes.
negative: Emit value changes before definitions.
positive: Inspect generated VCD section order and change records over increments with changed and unchanged variables.

edge: Use precision-sensitive shortreal values.
negative: Map shortreal to a fixed-width reg.
positive: Dump a shortreal and verify real value syntax and legacy real declaration.

edge: Attempt types absent from the supported mapping.
negative: Invent a new VCD var_type token for a SystemVerilog type.
positive: Dump each mapped SystemVerilog type and validate its emitted legacy var_type and size.

edge: Use each supported time magnitude and unit.
positive: Run with a known timescale and verify the VCD section reports it.

edge: Contrast a packed array with an unpacked array.
negative: Emit declarations or value changes for an unpacked array or automatic variable.
positive: Select a scope containing static scalar variables and verify those remain dumpable.

edge: Use nested unpacked structs.
negative: Flatten the unpacked struct into one packed vector.
positive: Dump an unpacked struct with heterogeneous members and verify fork scope plus individually mapped declarations.

edge: Return from the deepest nested scope to top through repeated commands.
negative: Move down or skip multiple levels for one $upscope.
positive: Parse nested $scope sections followed by $upscope and verify subsequent context.

edge: Compare uwire and wire declarations.
negative: Emit uwire as the VCD var_type token.
positive: Dump a uwire and verify its $var type token is wire.

edge: Use a one-bit significant suffix in a wide vector.
positive: Dump values narrower in significant content than their vector width and reconstruct by left extension.

edge: Use escaped identifiers.
positive: Compare VCD references to source variable identifiers across scopes.

edge: Use equal indices for a one-bit range.
positive: Compare declared ascending and descending design ranges with VCD msb/lsb fields.

edge: Declare scalar, wide vector, and real variables.
negative: Declare a vector with an incorrect size.
positive: Compare $var names, codes, and sizes against selected design variables.

edge: Represent all-zero, all-X, all-Z, and value beginning with 1.
negative: Remove a leading bit whose omission would reconstruct a different value.
positive: Dump vectors with long leading runs of 0, X, or Z and verify redundant prefix removal.

edge: Use uppercase B and a multi-character identifier code.
negative: Insert whitespace after the base letter or omit the separator before identifier.
positive: Validate records such as b1010 code with adjacency after b and one separator before code.

edge: Use a concatenated or variable filename expression.
negative: Replace an expression-form filename in version text solely with its evaluated value.
positive: Generate dumps with literal and expression filenames and inspect version text for writer and original task form.

edge: Compare selecting a single declared scalar with selecting one bit of a vector.
negative: Attempt to dump a part-select or expression such as a+b as a VCD object.
positive: Select a complete vector and verify its full width.

edge: Close at time zero and after a long quiet interval.
positive: Close an extended VCD at a known time with no simultaneous port change and verify that final time.

edge: Use final time #0.
negative: Omit the final time or $end.
positive: Parse $vcdclose #13000 $end.

edge: Use enum and wide packed integral indices.
negative: Pass a string-indexed associative array.
positive: Write a sparse integral-indexed associative array and verify an address for each emitted entry.

edge: Use explicitly assigned enum values and distinguish ordinal from encoded numeric value as defined by the clause.
negative: Write enum identifier names instead of numeric ordinal values.
positive: Write an enum array and verify file values correspond to each element's ordinal.

edge: Write a selected range with nonzero bounds.
negative: Emit address specifiers for a sequential array.
positive: Write unpacked fixed and dynamic arrays and verify no @ tokens occur.

edge: Overwrite a longer file with shorter output.
negative: Append new memory data after existing file content.
positive: Write to a preexisting file and verify all old trailing content is removed.

edge: Use packed widths not aligned to hexadecimal digits.
positive: Write unpacked arrays of packed structs and compare output with equivalent packed vectors.

edge: Use equal start and finish addresses.
negative: Supply finish_addr without start_addr.
positive: Invoke each task with two, three, and four arguments.

edge: Use four-state data spanning a 32-bit boundary.
positive: Write data wider than 32 bits with %z and verify the structure containing the LSB occurs first.

edge: Include X and Z bits in distinct native words.
notes: Expected bytes depend on host endianness and the standardized VPI vector representation.
positive: Write a multibit four-state value with %z and compare byte order to native s_vpi_vecval layout.

edge: Use a large aggregate that reaches the implementation's shared output limit.
notes: Do not require one exact short-form syntax.
positive: Format the same aggregate with %p and %0p and accept an implementation-specific shorter %0p representation.
